case_name: David Alias Balasaheb Sunderrao vs Kalpana Alias Mai Alias Vijayamala

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: husband, Indian Christian under the Indian Divorce Act
parties.respondent_defendant: wife, Kalpana Alias Mai Alias Vijayamala

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife committed frequent acts of adultery with co-respondent since December 6, 1970. Petitioner seeks decree declaring marriage null and void or in the alternative, a decree for divorce.

legal_principles.principle: A party can prove that their consent was obtained by fraud and entitle them to obtain a decree declaring the marriage null and void if false representations were made with the knowledge that they were false.
legal_principles.held: Mr. Sethna submitted that whatever be my view with regard to the sufficiency of evidence on the record, the main question is whether such false representations inducing consent on essential matters would enable a party to prove that his consent was obtained by fraud and further entitle him to obtain a decree declaring the marriage null and void.

legal_principles.principle: A party's right to obtain a decree for nullity can be lost due to acquiescence, approbation, condonation or waiver.
legal_principles.held: She submitted that even if such fraud is established, the Court has to consider the conduct of the petitioner and to see whether such right to obtain a decree for nullity is lost to the petitioner by reason of acquiescence, approbation, condonation or waiver.

outcome.final_order: Marriage declared null and void or decree of divorce may be passed in favour of the petitioner.
